summary.intent: Audit and reconcile Phase 70/70.1/71 todo drift against the roadmap, check Phase 72/73 dependencies, then plan, execute, and ship Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness) — with an emergent detour to diagnose and fix CI regressions and web-e2e flakiness that surfaced mid-flow before Phase 72 work could safely proceed.
summary.outcome: Retired 8 stale Phase 71 todos and updated ROADMAP for 72/73; fixed three CI regressions (FUSE seq-1 equivocation, stale test/fixture drift, sdk-e2e Test 21 flake) merged as PR #601 and #600; diagnosed and fixed 3 web-e2e timing flakes plus CI-timeout-asymmetry bugs; executed all 10 Phase 72 plans (SC#1–SC#6) across 7 waves with clean TDD, then fixed 113 pre-existing test-file TypeScript errors (vitest v2→v3 Mock migration + Phase-62 retired-type fallout) and wired a build-then-typecheck CI gate covering test files — final ship-phase step still pending at transcript end.

repo: GSD closes todos by deleting the file from pending/ and adding an identical copy to completed/ — there is no 'resolved/' folder in active use.

ci-e2e.yml (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch — never on pull_request — so PR authors must manually dispatch against their branch (`gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>`, not `-f ref=`) to get real e2e signal before merge.

Playwright's ciFloor() helper raises wait timeouts to 60s only under CI; local runs keep the raw (often 15s/30s) timeout, causing local-only cascading flakes on IPNS-gated mutations that pass fine in CI.

Setting CI=1 locally to get ciFloor's 60s regime also flips playwright.config.ts's `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI` to false, so it refuses to reuse an already-running stack — must temporarily patch reuse to true for accurate local CI-equivalent verification.

Root `pnpm typecheck` only ran each package's tsconfig.build.json (excludes tests) — test files were never typechecked in CI, letting 113 errors (vitest v3 Mock-generic breakage + Phase-62 retired-type imports) accumulate silently.

`@cipherbox/*` cross-package types resolve through the workspace symlink to each package's built `dist` (no path aliases/project references), so a package's typecheck needs upstream packages already built — hence typecheck must run build-first, per-package, in dependency order.

Phase 71 (#599) shipped with three separate pieces of undetected drift: a `.mts` desktop-e2e driver using pre-rename DTO field names, an sdk-e2e assertion incompatible with the phase's own idempotency guarantee, and a FUSE seq-1 publish bug newly exposed by its anti-equivocation gate.

Phase 70.1 collapsed two IndexedDB stores (`generation-high-water`+`seq-high-water`) into one `rotation-floor` store (DB v2) but left the e2e test helper pointed at the old store names, causing a silent short-circuit read.
`git commit` can appear to hang for ~2min due to a 1Password SSH-signing prompt during lint-staged — this is a known false-negative; the commit lands and the tree ends up clean.

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on the first-publish branch gated only by 'inode cid empty', so a dropped/stale UploadComplete re-running that branch re-seals at seq=1 with a new CID, tripping the anti-equivocation gate. Fixed by resolving IPNS before first-publish and routing 'Found' into the existing CAS-retry path with a preresolved_seq to avoid a redundant second resolve.

publish_with_cas_retry is the shared CAS helper for both file and folder publish; adding an optional preresolved_seq param let the first attempt skip a redundant resolve while the conflict-retry path still always re-resolves (pre-resolved value is stale after a conflict).

ciFloor() only raises wait timeouts under CI (60s), leaving local timeouts (15-30s) too tight for IPNS-gated batch mutations on this hardware, causing reproducible local-only cascading test failures unrelated to actual regressions.

getWriteBodyParams had a duplicated twin in bin/index.ts; both needed the same fail-closed fix for transient IPNS resolve misses, and were later unified into a shared write-body-params.ts module (Phase 72 SC#6 dedup) to eliminate the twin entirely.

Test 21 (D-06) asserted exactly one 200 + one 409 for concurrent same-CID first-publish, but Phase 71's own idempotency guarantee legitimately allows two 200s; the assertion needed to accept both outcomes while still rejecting genuine bugs (5xx, more than one rejection, non-409 rejections).

workflow: When a background local test run cascades on an unrelated flaky test, don't chase deeper into whack-a-mole fixes — switch to a CI-equivalent local regime (matching timeout floors) to get representative, non-cascading signal in one pass rather than iterating cold-stack conditions repeatedly.
When a PR fix's true validation only runs on main-push (not PRs), use workflow_dispatch against the fix branch to get pre-merge runtime proof instead of merging blind.
Sequencing a mechanical-but-broad hardening task (fixing all test-file TS drift + wiring a CI gate) as the LAST plan in a phase avoids redoing the fix after every subsequent wave adds new test files.
Raw hook-definition JSON files with embedded multiline string values aren't strict JSON — a lenient custom parser was needed to extract fragments rather than fighting JSON.parse.

User explicitly preferred build-then-typecheck ordering over typecheck-then-build once informed of the dist-based cross-package resolution constraint — simplicity given a real technical constraint beats a more 'ideal' ordering.

friction: Local web-e2e verification required 7 sequential background runs across ~2 hours because different tests (4.10, 4.11, 2.1) kept cascading due to tighter local timeouts than CI's ciFloor-raised ones, before finally getting a clean CI-equivalent pass.
Had to temporarily patch playwright.config.ts's webServer.reuseExistingServer to test under CI=1 locally, since CI mode otherwise refused to reuse the running dev stack.
Confusing/buggy git cat-file checks led to briefly believing todo completed/ counterparts were missing from HEAD when they weren't, requiring a decisive re-check.
gh workflow dispatch with `-f ref=` failed with HTTP 422 because main's workflow definition predated that input; had to discover the `--ref <branch>` alternative.
Executor subagent sandboxes couldn't access .env, deferring several live sdk-e2e test runs (bin-operations, TDD live confirmations) to be run manually at phase verification.
Wrote and debugged two custom Node scripts (extract-hook.cjs, lenient-parse.cjs) just to parse hook-definition JSON with embedded raw control characters.

Discovered the pre-existing test-file TS drift was larger and more complex than initially scoped — not just vitest v2→v3 Mock generics but full Phase-62 retired-type fallout in 12 sdk test files (62 errors).
